name: Spinach

molecules.name: Oxalic Acid
molecules.notes: Boiling spinach for 5 minutes and discarding water removes 30-87% of oxalates. Higher risk for those with kidney stones or low calcium intake.

molecules.name: Nitrate
molecules.notes: In healthy adults, dietary nitrate from vegetables is largely beneficial (vasodilatory, exercise performance). Risk is primarily for infants under 6 months (methemoglobinemia).

molecules.name: Vitamin K1 (Phylloquinone)
molecules.notes: Very high in Vitamin K1. Can interfere with warfarin (blood thinner) therapy — consistency of intake is key for anticoagulated patients.

molecules.name: Iron (non-heme)
molecules.notes: Non-heme iron absorption is inhibited by the same oxalic acid also present in spinach. Pair with vitamin C to improve absorption.

preparation_notes: Boil or blanch and discard water to reduce oxalates. Avoid feeding large amounts to infants. Those with kidney stones or on warfarin should consult a doctor.
